facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Reported-basis leverage peaked one quarter after closing and has fallen since: total debt to EBITDA was 4.23x at 2026-03-31, 3.80x at 2026-06-30 and 3.31x at 2026-09-30, against 2.83x at year-end 2025. Debt fell by USD 255 million over the last two of those quarters while last-twelve-months reported EBITDA rose from USD 1,009 million to USD 1,211 million as acquired quarters replaced pre-closing ones, so part of the improvement is arithmetic and continues only if the acquired business keeps earning at the 2026 rate. Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_alsn-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation TD-6; calculation LT-4; calculation LT-6

facts.text: Interest cover is the pressure point. Action: obtain pre-closing quarterly EBITDA or a management bridge. - Cash flow lines that the sources print as a dash, or do not print for a period, are shown as not supplied and never as zero: business acquisition, revolver proceeds and payments, issuance of long-term debt, debt financing fees and the foreign exchange effect for periods before 2026, and the same revolver and acquisition lines in the fiscal-year columns. They restrict only the line-by-line view; the activity totals tie to the change in cash. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for the totals. - Segment net sales, operating profit and adjusted EBITDA for the fiscal years 2023 to 2025 are not supplied because the annual report presents one segment, and segment adjusted EBITDA for the second quarter, third quarter, half year and nine months of 2025 is not stated; the Off-Highway business has no 2025 figures. This restricts the segment trend before 2026. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the recast annual segment data. - The first-quarter earnings release states total debt of 4,292 and net debt of 3,981 that match neither the quarterly report carrying value of 4,267 nor its principal of 4,295, and its balance sheet shows total assets 46 above the quarterly report. The quarterly report is used for every first-quarter figure. Severity: Medium. Action: confirm with the issuer which figure the release used. - No instrument-level carrying values are disclosed; only aggregate deferred financing costs of 25 are stated, so the debt table shows principal and one financing cost adjustment. Finance lease liabilities of 38 carry no stated ranking or security and are left out of the debt stack, and the ranking of the notes among themselves and below the secured facilities rests on the stated unsecured status. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the indentures and credit agreement. - The maturity ladder at 2026-09-30 is calculated: the quarterly report gives no printed ladder, and the five-year ladder in the annual report predates the incremental term loan. Scheduled payments are the stated minimums of 1 on the term loan and 3 on the incremental term loan, assumed paid at quarter ends. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the amortisation schedules. - The adjusted EBITDA add-back called Other, 7 in the nine months, is defined by the credit agreement, which is not supplied, and no add-back carries a stated realisation status. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the credit agreement definitions. - The fourth quarter of 2025 is constructed as the fiscal year less nine months because no fourth-quarter release is supplied, and revolver availability at 2024-12-31 is not stated in the 2025 annual report. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the fourth-quarter release and the 2024 annual report. - The acquisition purchase price is approximately 2,732 in the annual report and 2,628 in the quarterly reports, a difference of 104 that no source bridges. The quarterly figure ties to the cash flow statement and is used. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for the figures used. - Marketable securities of 24 at 2025-12-31 appear on their own line in the annual report and inside other non-current assets in later reports, so those two columns are not on one presentation. Severity: Low. Action: none needed. - Cash held by foreign subsidiaries of 361 at 2026-09-30 may not be freely available to the borrower, and no source states any restriction beyond the issuer's remark that local restrictions are not expected to prevent funding. Severity: Low. Action: monitor.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The purchase was funded almost entirely with new debt, and the new money is mostly secured, which moves existing noteholders further back. New principal of USD 2,000 million (a USD 1,200 million incremental term loan, USD 500 million of unsecured notes and a USD 300 million revolver draw) covered all but USD 628 million of the price, and cash fell from USD 1,495 million at year-end 2025 to USD 263 million after closing. Secured term debt rose by USD 1,190 million to USD 1,699 million, against USD 2,300 million of unsecured notes, so noteholders now sit behind a much larger secured tranche. facts.text: The legacy business is the anchor of the credit. Allison Transmission net sales rose 8.84% in the nine months, defense sales rose 44.33%, and North American on-highway is 51.21% of segment sales under long-term agreements that cover over 90% of its unit volume. facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The purchase was funded with new debt and cash. Allison Transmission, Inc. issued USD 500 million of senior unsecured notes due December 2033 in November 2025. On 2026-01-02 it added a USD 1,200 million secured incremental term loan due 2033-01-02 at Term SOFR plus 1.75% (5.54% all-in at 2026-09-30), raised the revolver commitments from USD 750 million to USD 1,000 million with a January 2031 maturity and drew USD 300 million. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view

facts.label: Qualitative downside scenario
facts.text: The issuer-specific downside begins with a North American truck downturn like 2025, when legacy net sales fell 6.67%, arriving while agriculture and industrial demand stay subdued. The first operational break is volume against a cost base that is about 29% overhead, followed by under-absorption at the acquired plants where the margin is only 14.03%. Financial transmission runs through EBITDA to interest cover, which is already 6.55x on the last twelve months and 5.94x on run-rate interest, with USD 1,699 million of floating-rate debt unhedged and USD 195 million of nine-month shareholder returns continuing unless cut. Management levers are suspending buybacks, trimming capital expenditure and the revolver, with liquidity of USD 1,493 million, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity problem before the USD 300 million 2027 notes fall due, but deleveraging would stall and the observable triggers are a fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA below USD 364 million and an Off-Highway margin below 14.03%. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Allison presents an adequate business profile supported by a high-margin transmission franchise, long-term OEM agreements and a large aftermarket, but credit quality is constrained by acquisition leverage of 3.31x, interest cover of 6.55x and an unproven lower-margin Off-Highway business. Cash-flow durability appears adequate due to free cash flow of USD 662 million in nine months and cost actions that held margin in 2025. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on continued repayment, stable ratings and the 2029 and 2031 maturities. The primary downside path is a North American truck downturn coinciding with weak off-highway demand. Further analysis would require pro forma EBITDA, the executed debt documents and ownership detail. Top risk: a cyclical volume decline that stalls deleveraging while interest and shareholder returns continue. ## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven supplied filings and releases support a credit snapshot of Allison Transmission Holdings Inc as of 5 November 2026, so creditors can rely on the filed debt, liquidity and covenant figures but not on pro forma leverage or legal-document terms.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–22; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C-01; calculation C-02

## Request

Issuer: Allison Transmission Holdings Inc (issuer id alsn), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot. Scope: the financial foundation (statements, debt, liquidity, leverage and coverage) built from the seven supplied filings and releases and the Source readiness handoff.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Total debt to reported EBITDA rose from 2.83x at year-end 2025 to 3.31x at 2026-09-30 after the Off-Highway purchase, so creditors now depend on acquired earnings and further debt repayment, although this ratio overstates run-rate leverage.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation LT-6; calculation TD-5

Net debt is USD 2,120 million higher than at year-end 2025 and cash interest cover fell from 8.50x to 6.55x, yet nine-month free cash flow of USD 662 million, debt repayment of USD 410 million and liquidity of USD 1,493 million show the debt is being serviced and reduced.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 44; calculation ND-6; calculation FC-1; calculation DR-1; calculation LQ-1
No pro forma EBITDA is supplied, so combined leverage is not established; net debt is 2.46x adjusted EBITDA, and only USD 320 million of debt matures through 2027.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation LD-2; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Key findings

Reported-basis leverage peaked one quarter after closing and has fallen since: total debt to EBITDA was 4.23x at 2026-03-31, 3.80x at 2026-06-30 and 3.31x at 2026-09-30, against 2.83x at year-end 2025. Debt fell by USD 255 million over the last two of those quarters while last-twelve-months reported EBITDA rose from USD 1,009 million to USD 1,211 million as acquired quarters replaced pre-closing ones, so part of the improvement is arithmetic and continues only if the acquired business keeps earning at the 2026 rate.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_alsn-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation TD-6; calculation LT-4; calculation LT-6

Interest cover is the pressure point. EBITDA to cash interest paid was 8.50x in FY2025 and 6.55x over the last twelve months, and net interest expense of USD 51 million in Q3 alone annualises to USD 204 million, which would put run-rate cover at 5.94x on reported-basis EBITDA and 7.01x on adjusted EBITDA. Floating-rate term debt of USD 1,699 million carries the rate exposure, and the twelve-month cash interest figure still includes a quarter before the acquisition debt was drawn.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 19–20; calculation IC-1; calculation IC-2; calculation IC-3; calculation FR-1

Free cash flow of USD 662 million in the nine months, 65.74% of reported EBITDA, covered USD 410 million of debt repayment and USD 195 million returned to shareholders; the twelve-month figure is USD 831 million. Cash generation is therefore the deleveraging engine, so a working-capital reversal or faster buybacks would slow it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation FC-1; calculation FC-2; calculation FC-3; calculation DR-1; calculation CR-1

Liquidity at 2026-09-30 is USD 1,493 million, made up of USD 497 million of cash and USD 996 million of undrawn revolver commitments, against USD 4 million of debt due in the rest of 2026 and USD 316 million in 2027. Most of the cash is offshore: USD 361 million, or 72.64%, is held by foreign subsidiaries, so domestic cash is about USD 136 million and the cushion available in the United States is the revolver, which matures in January 2031.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 44; calculation LQ-1; calculation LQ-2; calculation LQ-3

Maturities are back-ended. Only USD 320 million falls due before 2028 and 78.29% of principal matures in 2031 or later, so the first bond maturity of consequence is the USD 500 million of 2029 notes, which falls in a year with USD 516 million of principal due.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; calculation LD-1; calculation LD-2; calculation LD-3

Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,166 million in the nine months is USD 159 million, or 13.64%, above reported-basis EBITDA of USD 1,007 million. Most of the gap is purchase accounting (USD 64 million of inventory step-up) and acquisition costs (USD 30 million), but the issuer states no realisation status for any add-back and defines the Other line of USD 7 million by an agreement that is not supplied, so adjusted measures are shown beside the reported basis, not in place of it.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation BR-1; calculation BR-2

Mix dilutes margins. Allison Off-Highway earned a nine-month adjusted EBITDA margin of 14.03% against 37.47% for Allison Transmission, and the consolidated margin fell to 25.88% from 38.06% a year earlier, so coverage now rests partly on a lower-margin business whose agriculture and industrial end markets the issuer calls subdued. Allison Transmission's own net sales rose 8.84%.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 8, 10; calculation SG-1; calculation SG-2; calculation SG-3; calculation SG-4; calculation GR-2

The acquisition closed on 2026-01-01 and its financing, a USD 1,200 million incremental term loan and a USD 300 million revolver draw, is dated 2026-01-02, both after the 2025-12-31 balance sheet. Year-end 2025 net debt of USD 1,395 million (1.37x) is therefore not a guide to current leverage, and no event after 2026-09-30 changes net debt in the sources read.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 65, 118; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; calculation ND-2

Customer-funded float is small: deferred revenue was USD 179 million at 2026-09-30, mostly extended transmission coverage, against USD 4,012 million of debt, and no supplier finance or receivables sale programme appears in the filings read.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 25; calculation DF-1; calculation TD-5
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case that leverage is lower than it looks: the reported-basis ratio uses a twelve-month period that includes a quarter before the acquired business, net debt is 2.46x adjusted EBITDA, and the first lien net leverage ratio the issuer reports is 0.84x against a 5.50x maximum. If the acquired business sustains its nine-month margin and free cash flow stays near USD 662 million for nine months, leverage on a full-year basis would fall faster than the last-twelve-months ratios show.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; calculation FC-1; calculation LT-6

The view turns more cautious on an Off-Highway margin below the 14.03% earned in the nine months, a redraw of the revolver or repayment slower than the USD 255 million of debt reduction over the last two quarters, buybacks above free cash flow, or cash interest running at the annualised USD 204 million rather than the last-twelve-months USD 185 million.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation SG-2; calculation TD-6; calculation IC-1
### Limitations

- No pro forma adjusted EBITDA or pre-closing quarterly EBITDA for the acquired business is supplied, so combined leverage and cover are not established and every last-twelve-months ratio combines a quarter before the acquisition with quarters after it.

- Reported EBITDA is calculated from components because the issuer states only an adjusted measure defined by a credit agreement that is not supplied, so the covenant ratio of 0.84x cannot be reproduced from the sources.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22

- The maturity ladder is calculated from stated maturities and minimum quarterly payments, and the ranking of the notes below the secured facilities rests on their stated unsecured status, because no printed ladder at 2026-09-30 and no ranking statement is supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–22

- The first-quarter earnings release disagrees with the first-quarter quarterly report on total debt of USD 4,292 million against USD 4,267 million and on total assets of USD 8,749 million against USD 8,703 million; the quarterly report is used.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-05-04_d138525dex991.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 8; 10-Q_2026-03-31_alsn-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation RL-1; calculation RL-2

- Interim statements are unaudited, purchase accounting stays preliminary until the one-year measurement period ends, and the fourth quarter of 2025 is constructed as the year less nine months because no fourth-quarter release is supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; calculation Q4-1

## Gaps

- Pro forma earnings for the combined business are not supplied. The filings print pro forma net sales and net income for the third quarter and nine months but no pro forma adjusted EBITDA and no quarterly EBITDA for the acquired business before closing, so every last-twelve-months ratio combines a quarter without the acquired business with quarters that include it and combined leverage is not established. Severity: High. Action: obtain pre-closing quarterly EBITDA or a management bridge.

- Cash flow lines that the sources print as a dash, or do not print for a period, are shown as not supplied and never as zero: business acquisition, revolver proceeds and payments, issuance of long-term debt, debt financing fees and the foreign exchange effect for periods before 2026, and the same revolver and acquisition lines in the fiscal-year columns. They restrict only the line-by-line view; the activity totals tie to the change in cash. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for the totals.

- Segment net sales, operating profit and adjusted EBITDA for the fiscal years 2023 to 2025 are not supplied because the annual report presents one segment, and segment adjusted EBITDA for the second quarter, third quarter, half year and nine months of 2025 is not stated; the Off-Highway business has no 2025 figures. This restricts the segment trend before 2026. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the recast annual segment data.

- The first-quarter earnings release states total debt of 4,292 and net debt of 3,981 that match neither the quarterly report carrying value of 4,267 nor its principal of 4,295, and its balance sheet shows total assets 46 above the quarterly report. The quarterly report is used for every first-quarter figure. Severity: Medium. Action: confirm with the issuer which figure the release used.

- No instrument-level carrying values are disclosed; only aggregate deferred financing costs of 25 are stated, so the debt table shows principal and one financing cost adjustment. Finance lease liabilities of 38 carry no stated ranking or security and are left out of the debt stack, and the ranking of the notes among themselves and below the secured facilities rests on the stated unsecured status. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the indentures and credit agreement.

- The maturity ladder at 2026-09-30 is calculated: the quarterly report gives no printed ladder, and the five-year ladder in the annual report predates the incremental term loan. Scheduled payments are the stated minimums of 1 on the term loan and 3 on the incremental term loan, assumed paid at quarter ends. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the amortisation schedules.

- The adjusted EBITDA add-back called Other, 7 in the nine months, is defined by the credit agreement, which is not supplied, and no add-back carries a stated realisation status. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the credit agreement definitions.

- The fourth quarter of 2025 is constructed as the fiscal year less nine months because no fourth-quarter release is supplied, and revolver availability at 2024-12-31 is not stated in the 2025 annual report. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the fourth-quarter release and the 2024 annual report.

- The acquisition purchase price is approximately 2,732 in the annual report and 2,628 in the quarterly reports, a difference of 104 that no source bridges. The quarterly figure ties to the cash flow statement and is used. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for the figures used.

- Marketable securities of 24 at 2025-12-31 appear on their own line in the annual report and inside other non-current assets in later reports, so those two columns are not on one presentation. Severity: Low. Action: none needed.

- Cash held by foreign subsidiaries of 361 at 2026-09-30 may not be freely available to the borrower, and no source states any restriction beyond the issuer's remark that local restrictions are not expected to prevent funding. Severity: Low. Action: monitor.

## Findings
### Bottom line

After the USD 2,628 million Off-Highway purchase, Allison is a more diversified but lower-margin group with no sponsor, so creditors rely on observed behaviour, which has been broadly supportive, rather than on legal documents that are not supplied.

### Key findings

The purchase was funded almost entirely with new debt, and the new money is mostly secured, which moves existing noteholders further back. New principal of USD 2,000 million (a USD 1,200 million incremental term loan, USD 500 million of unsecured notes and a USD 300 million revolver draw) covered all but USD 628 million of the price, and cash fell from USD 1,495 million at year-end 2025 to USD 263 million after closing. Secured term debt rose by USD 1,190 million to USD 1,699 million, against USD 2,300 million of unsecured notes, so noteholders now sit behind a much larger secured tranche.

Diversification is real but of lower quality than the legacy franchise. Off-Highway is 45.10% of nine-month net sales, spread across construction and material handling at 34.84%, agriculture at 21.46%, industrial at 13.83%, mining at 7.73% and service parts, specialty and other at 22.15%, but it earns an adjusted EBITDA margin of 14.03% against 37.47% for Allison Transmission, and the issuer calls agriculture and industrial demand subdued. Implied pro forma sales growth was 4.15% in the third quarter and 7.57% in the nine months, so the acquisition has not yet shown strong underlying growth.

The legacy business is the anchor of the credit. Allison Transmission net sales rose 8.84% in the nine months, defense sales rose 44.33%, and North American on-highway is 51.21% of segment sales under long-term agreements that cover over 90% of its unit volume. That strength comes with concentration: the top three OEM customers were 39% of 2025 net sales and the top five about 52%, so the loss of one customer or a turn in the truck cycle would hit cash flow directly.

Management has repaid debt while still returning cash: USD 410 million of debt was repaid in the nine months against USD 195 million returned to shareholders, the dividend was raised for the seventh consecutive year and USD 1,068 million of buyback authority remains. The stated net leverage target of 2.0x has no definition or date, so creditors cannot hold management to a timetable, which is the main reason governance risk is rated Medium rather than Low.

There is no sponsor, so the usual extraction routes (dividend recapitalisations, monitoring fees, sponsor-led amendments) are not documented. Ownership is widely dispersed among public holders and one person is Chair, President and Chief Executive Officer, but the proxy statement that would show five-percent holders, board independence and committees and related-party dealings is not supplied. The absence of a sponsor removes one risk and leaves board control unassessed.

Integration costs are front-loaded. The issuer guides about USD 125 million of one-time pre-tax expense for 2026, including about USD 65 million of inventory step-up, booked a USD 17 million restructuring charge in the third quarter, and carries goodwill and intangibles of USD 1,645 million, 62.60% of the price, on a preliminary basis. If Off-Highway margins stay near 14.03% that balance becomes an impairment question, and the USD 29 million write-down of electrified-product assets in 2025 shows the issuer has taken such charges before.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The view that the diversification is of lower quality could be too harsh: Off-Highway has only three quarters in the numbers, the issuer says construction and mining demand is rebounding from trough levels and the third quarter is seasonally the softest, and the legacy business is at record sales with a 37.47% margin. If integration lifts the Off-Highway margin toward the legacy level, group cash generation would be stronger than the nine-month figures show.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Allison Transmission Holdings completed the purchase of Dana Incorporated's off-highway business on 2026-01-01 under a stock purchase agreement signed on 2025-06-11. The final price was USD 2,628 million: USD 2,664 million of cash was transferred at closing, USD 2 million of it settling an existing payable, and a USD 34 million post-closing adjustment came back. The annual report gave approximately USD 2,732 million and no source bridges the USD 104 million difference.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 117–118; calculation FD-4; calculation FD-5

The purchase was funded with new debt and cash. Allison Transmission, Inc. issued USD 500 million of senior unsecured notes due December 2033 in November 2025. On 2026-01-02 it added a USD 1,200 million secured incremental term loan due 2033-01-02 at Term SOFR plus 1.75% (5.54% all-in at 2026-09-30), raised the revolver commitments from USD 750 million to USD 1,000 million with a January 2031 maturity and drew USD 300 million. A 364-day bridge commitment of up to USD 2,000 million, cut to USD 500 million by year-end 2025, was never drawn and ended at closing, and cash on hand covered the rest, falling from USD 1,495 million to USD 263 million.

- The executed credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so legal capacity for restricted payments, debt, liens, asset transfers and amendments is not established, and behaviour is judged from actions only. Severity: High. Action: obtain the executed documents and amendments.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Allison's credit profile is adequate but weaker than before the Off-Highway purchase: a high-margin transmission franchise generates the cash to reduce acquisition debt, so creditors are exposed mainly to cycle and integration risk.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation FC-1; calculation MG-5

On a reported basis total debt is 3.31x EBITDA and cash interest cover is 6.55x, against 2.83x and 8.50x at year-end 2025, and both are distorted by a last-twelve-months period that includes a quarter before the acquisition. Free cash flow of USD 662 million in nine months and liquidity of USD 1,493 million leave room to keep repaying debt.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation LV-1; calculation LV-2; calculation CV-1; calculation CV-2; calculation FC-1; calculation LQ-1

The primary downside is a North American truck downturn that coincides with weak agriculture and industrial demand at Off-Highway while buybacks and floating-rate interest continue; pro forma EBITDA, executed debt documents and ownership detail are not supplied, so conviction is limited.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 1
### Key findings

The legacy transmission franchise is the main support and held its margin through a down year. Allison Transmission earned an adjusted EBITDA margin of 37.47% in the nine months, and in 2025 net sales fell 6.67% while adjusted EBITDA fell only 3.00%, lifting the margin from 36.12% to 37.54%. Long-term agreements cover over 90% of North American on-highway unit volume and service parts, support equipment and other sales were 21% of 2025 revenue, so contracted volumes and replacement demand cushion a mild downturn.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 80; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation MG-1; calculation MG-2; calculation MG-3; calculation MG-4; calculation MG-5

Leverage is higher and the improvement so far is partly arithmetic. Total debt to reported EBITDA was 4.23x at 2026-03-31 and 3.31x at 2026-09-30, against 2.83x at year-end 2025, with debt down USD 255 million over the two quarters and last-twelve-months EBITDA rising as acquired quarters replaced pre-closing ones. On the issuer's adjusted measure net debt is 2.46x EBITDA, so true leverage may be lower than the reported ratio suggests, although no pro forma figure confirms that.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation LV-1; calculation LV-2; calculation LV-3; calculation LV-7; calculation LV-8

Interest cover is the weakest financial metric and will not recover quickly. EBITDA covered cash interest 6.55x over the last twelve months against 8.50x in 2025, and net interest expense of USD 51 million in the third quarter annualises to USD 204 million, which puts run-rate cover at 5.94x. The USD 1,699 million of floating-rate term debt has no swaps, so each 1% rise in rates adds USD 16.99 million of interest.

### Company description

Allison makes fully automatic transmissions and electric propulsion solutions for commercial vehicles, buses, motorhomes and U.S. defense vehicles, sells service parts and extended coverage through a network of independent distributors and dealers, and since 2026-01-01 also makes drivetrain and motion systems for construction, agriculture, mining, material handling and industrial equipment. The legacy business is cash generative and contractually anchored, while the acquired business broadens end markets at lower margins, so the model supports debt service but with a larger share of cyclical, lower-margin revenue than before.

Revenue is cyclical and OEM-driven but contract-supported: North American on-highway is 51.21% of legacy sales, long-term agreements cover over 90% of its unit volume with pricing and commodity cost sharing, and the top five OEM customers were about 52% of 2025 sales. ### Porter's Five Forces

- Rivalry is limited in North American on-highway, where Allison supplies the fully automatic transmission, but vertically integrated OEMs and competitors such as Caterpillar, Komatsu and Volvo cap share in mining and construction, which limits growth at Off-Highway.

- New entrants face high engineering and manufacturing barriers, and fully electric propulsion remains in a developmental phase for medium- and heavy-duty vehicles, so electrification is a long-dated rather than near-term threat to cash flow.
- Substitutes are manual and automated manual transmissions, mainly in Class 8 line-haul where Allison has limited exposure, so substitution risk is concentrated in a small part of sales.
- Buyer power is high because a handful of OEMs buy most volume, offset by long-term agreements and by end users who often specify the Allison product.
- Supplier power matters through aluminium and steel castings and forgings and a direct-material share of about 65% of cost of sales that passes through only in part.
### PEST analysis

Political and economic factors are material to credit: defense spending and trade protectionism are named risks, defense sales rose 44.33% in nine months, and foreign-currency exposure from the acquisition is partly hedged through cross-currency swaps and forwards. Social and technological factors, mainly electrification, do not appear to be a primary credit driver within the horizon of the provided materials.
### SWOT
- Strengths: a 37.47% legacy margin, long-term OEM agreements, a sizeable aftermarket, record legacy sales and USD 1,493 million of liquidity.
- Weaknesses: leverage of 3.31x on reported EBITDA, interest cover of 6.55x, customer concentration, unhedged floating-rate debt and a lower-margin acquired business.
- Opportunities: integration savings and rebounding construction and mining demand at Off-Highway, and continued growth in defense.
- Threats: a truck-cycle downturn, subdued agriculture and industrial demand, tariffs and trade policy, and impairment of acquired intangibles.

### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale and market position, and competitive advantage, are assessed as strong because Allison is the largest maker of fully automatic transmissions for its core markets and earns a 37.47% margin. Business diversification, cost and capex flexibility, margin stability, free cash flow stability, the ability to refinance and liquidity are average: the acquisition broadened end markets but at a 14.03% margin, cost actions held margin in 2025, free cash flow is 65.74% of EBITDA, maturities are distant but leverage is 3.31x, and liquidity is USD 1,493 million with thin domestic cash. Financial policy and governance is average because debt is being repaid while USD 195 million was returned to shareholders and the leverage target is undefined. The trend is improving from a peak of 4.23x at 2026-03-31, and the key missing datapoints are pro forma EBITDA, the debt documents and ownership detail.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months the issuer has raised 2026 guidance twice, to net sales of USD 5,975 million to USD 6,075 million, adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,530 million to USD 1,580 million and adjusted free cash flow of USD 850 million to USD 900 million, which implies fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA of USD 364 million to USD 414 million against USD 400 million in the third quarter, so the guidance allows a modest decline or a modest rise. Tailwinds are record legacy sales, defense growth and rebounding construction and mining demand; headwinds are subdued agriculture and industrial demand, integration costs of about USD 125 million of one-time expense and tariffs. Beyond two years no company plan is supplied, so the medium-term view rests on the long-term agreements, the aftermarket and the maturity profile, with electrification a longer-dated risk.

### Qualitative downside scenario

The issuer-specific downside begins with a North American truck downturn like 2025, when legacy net sales fell 6.67%, arriving while agriculture and industrial demand stay subdued. The first operational break is volume against a cost base that is about 29% overhead, followed by under-absorption at the acquired plants where the margin is only 14.03%. Financial transmission runs through EBITDA to interest cover, which is already 6.55x on the last twelve months and 5.94x on run-rate interest, with USD 1,699 million of floating-rate debt unhedged and USD 195 million of nine-month shareholder returns continuing unless cut. Management levers are suspending buybacks, trimming capital expenditure and the revolver, with liquidity of USD 1,493 million, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity problem before the USD 300 million 2027 notes fall due, but deleveraging would stall and the observable triggers are a fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA below USD 364 million and an Off-Highway margin below 14.03%.

### Overall credit view

Overall, Allison presents an adequate business profile supported by a high-margin transmission franchise, long-term OEM agreements and a large aftermarket, but credit quality is constrained by acquisition leverage of 3.31x, interest cover of 6.55x and an unproven lower-margin Off-Highway business. Cash-flow durability appears adequate due to free cash flow of USD 662 million in nine months and cost actions that held margin in 2025. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on continued repayment, stable ratings and the 2029 and 2031 maturities. The primary downside path is a North American truck downturn coinciding with weak off-highway demand. Further analysis would require pro forma EBITDA, the executed debt documents and ownership detail. Top risk: a cyclical volume decline that stalls deleveraging while interest and shareholder returns continue.
